answer: At the old weighhouse a claim settles only when one real town withdraws its own stamp for good: the iron that certifies its weights is struck from service, dated in the roll of withdrawn stamps, and that town can never certify anything again, not for a second head and not for itself. What the head spends is not money but a whole town's capacity to vouch, and the roll shows one address collecting stamp after stamp, so honest towns keep their iron in service. A zephyr of hollow guarantees fills no nebula of settled claims.
